notes: For each permutation pi, its initial segments form a chain, hence meet the antichain A in at most one set. A k-set is an initial segment in exactly k!(n-k)! permutations. Double counting gives sum_{A in A} 1/binom(n,|A|)<=1. The ratio binom(n,k+1)/binom(n,k)=(n-k)/(k+1) proves the maximum binomial coefficient occurs at floor(n/2) (also at ceil(n/2) when n odd). Thus |A|/M<=LYM sum<=1. Equality example is the full floor(n/2)-level.
